amended.note: The four claims added on 2026-07-25 were captured on the same toolchain, host, and operating-system build recorded below, verified identical before the run: rustc eff8269f797067c30555e77f160ec84c0ed15cd9, cargo 3efb1f477e99b42974b982d939fd100303cdf7db, aarch64-apple-darwin, macOS 27.0 (26A5388g). The record stays one file because the verifier requires the recorded fixture set to equal the set on disk in both directions, so a second record would have to restate every claim in this one.

claims.statement: A total map over a #[non_exhaustive] enum inside the defining crate compiles with no wildcard arm.
The same total map in a consuming crate fails E0004 because the attribute makes a wildcard arm mandatory.
required_fragments: `Growing` is marked as non-exhaustive, so a wildcard `_` is necessary to match exhaustively

claims.statement: With #![feature(non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns_lint)], #[deny(non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns)] turns an omitted known variant back into a hard cross-crate compile error.
claims.first_line: error: some variants are not matched explicitly

claims.statement: Without the feature gate the lint name is unknown, so the attribute constrains nothing and the omitted variant is never reported; only unknown_lints fires.
required_fragments: add `#![feature(non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns_lint)]` to the crate attributes to enable
forbidden_fragments: some variants are not matched explicitly

claims.statement: The unknown lint is warning level by default: the same omission compiles when unknown_lints is not denied. The sibling fail case denies it, which is what the repository gate's -D warnings does.
A cross-crate recognizer that carries the mandatory wildcard compiles, and nothing reports the variant it never named.
The denied lint accepts a match that keeps its wildcard and also names every variant; that is the form a consumer would have to maintain.

A discriminant cast of a #[non_exhaustive] enum written outside the defining crate compiles. The attribute does not constrain `as`, so it cannot reach an encoder that reads a tag from ordinal position.

The same total map written as the convention-3 match, deriving the same tag for the same variant across the same crate boundary, fails E0004. The pair is the measurement: the attribute reaches the written match and not the cast, so convention 3 rather than convention 5 is what closes a discriminant-cast encoder.
required_fragments: `Growing` is marked as non-exhaustive, so a wildcard `_` is necessary to match exhaustively
the matched value is of type `Growing`

claims.statement: A crate that enables non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns_lint and denies the lint crate-wide still compiles a cross-crate discriminant cast. The escape hatch ADR 0074 records as the alternative to dropping #[non_exhaustive] is a lint about match arms, and a cast writes none, so a stricter lint level does not close the hole either.

The control for the claim above. A compiling fixture cannot distinguish a lint that does not reach a cast from a crate-level lint level the compiler accepts and never consults, and the pre-existing denied case only rules that out for a #[deny] written on the match itself, which no cast site has. This fixture denies the lint at crate level and contains both constructs: the retained diagnostic reports the omitting match, names the crate-level attribute as the level that fired, and says nothing about the cast beside it.
